museums.content_summary: Baltimore Museum of Art is one of the Mid-Atlantic’s essential art stops, pairing a nationally respected collection with a visitor-friendly campus setting. Come for a deep, beautifully installed survey of modern and contemporary art—especially the museum’s renowned holdings of Henri Matisse—then stay for standout galleries of prints, photography, and global works. With strong regional curatorial authority and an experience designed for looking closely, it’s a museum that rewards both first-time visitors and serious art lovers.
museums.content_description:
**The Baltimore Museum of Art (BMA)** is a must for travelers who want a museum visit that feels both intellectually serious and genuinely pleasurable. Set in Baltimore’s Charles Village area near Johns Hopkins University, the BMA offers the kind of calm, spacious viewing experience that art lovers crave—galleries with room to linger, clear sightlines, and thoughtful wall texts that support close looking without getting in the way. The museum’s reputation rests on its **major scholarly holdings**, and its installations excel at making big art-historical ideas legible in the moment: how *modernism* breaks from tradition, how *abstraction* evolves, and how contemporary artists expand what a museum can be.

Collection-wise, the BMA is particularly celebrated for **Henri Matisse**—a defining strength that draws visitors who want to study the artist beyond a single famous canvas. You’ll also find robust presentations of **modern and contemporary art**, complemented by strong resources in prints, drawings, and photography that reward repeat visits (and provide a quieter, more intimate counterpoint to the large-galleries “greatest hits” rhythm). As a museum with **strong regional curatorial authority**, the BMA also makes Baltimore and the broader American story feel present—through collecting choices, exhibitions, and interpretive framing that connect art to the civic and social fabric.

Architecturally, the BMA reads as a composed museum campus rather than a one-room monument, emphasizing **light, scale, and legibility**—an environment that supports long, focused looking. For visitors, the pleasures are tangible: planned routes that can be tackled in a single afternoon, galleries that encourage comparative viewing across periods, and a sense that the museum is both nationally significant and unmistakably rooted in place.
content_highlights: Renowned Henri Matisse holdings—one of the BMA’s signature strengths and a major draw for modern art fans
Strong modern and contemporary art installations that make key developments in abstraction and postwar art easy to follow
Deep resources in prints, drawings, and photography—ideal for close looking and repeat visits
Thoughtful, scholarship-forward curation with a distinctly Baltimore perspective and strong regional authority
A spacious, light-filled museum campus experience that supports unhurried viewing and easy self-guided itineraries

google_reviews.text:
This place completely exceeded my expectations. I really had no idea what I was getting into, and the Baltimore Museum of Art turned out to be deceivingly massive. From the outside you’d never guess how much is packed inside. You could easily spend an entire day here  and honestly, you should  just to take everything in without rushing.
They have this interactive section that’s actually fun (not one of those awkward “pretend to touch this screen” situations), and the historic art rooms are stunning. You walk in and it feels like you’ve stepped into another time. There’s a sculpture garden too I didn’t even make it that far because there was just so much to see plus entire areas dedicated to Mediterranean art, European pieces, and these beautifully curated exhibits that really pull you in.
One thing I loved is how organized everything is. The museum feels intentional, thoughtful, and incredibly well put together. Even the flow from room to room makes sense, which is rare for a museum this big.
Overall, it’s just an extraordinary place. If you’re anywhere near Baltimore, this is absolutely worth your time. I genuinely can’t recommend it enough it’s incredible.
It was so fantastic the fact it's free is extra cool. The area is super nice! They had so many different types of art you could take days to explore.

Our first time visit ( and we live in relative close vincinty for 20+ years. Shame on us). What a gem of a art museum. Not the MET of course....but on a smaller scale. Worth a visit. Actually worth multiple visits.
Note: parking lots on site are very small so get there early for a spot or plan to park on the street in close vincinty which is perfectly fine. You just walk a short bit.

Also... Gertrude's restaurant on site is wonderful.

I’ve visited the Baltimore Museum of Art a few times over the years and always enjoy the experience. I went recently to see the Amy Sherald: American Sublime exhibition, which is open until April 5, 2026. It’s a popular show with timed entry tickets ($18 + tax/fees for adults; free for members).

I was able to find paid street parking right in front of the museum, and there’s also a dedicated paid lot.
Check in at the front desk when you walk in, and the team will point you toward the exhibition. It’s up a few flights of stairs if you prefer to walk, and there’s an elevator route as well.

The lobby currently features a colorful, quirky display of large-scale abstract figures covered in beads. Throughout the museum, there’s a wide mix of modern and classical works, and the layout flows nicely through different galleries and a central courtyard. It’s a beautiful building and very thoughtfully curated.

Since my visit was focused on American Sublime, a few highlights:
Once your ticket is scanned at the entrance, you’re immediately met with bold color, striking compositions, and larger-than-life portraits of African American subjects in distinctive attire. The standout pieces include the iconic portrait of former First Lady Michelle Obama and the moving tribute to Breonna Taylor. The short film about Amy Sherald at the end is absolutely worth watching for more insight into her process.

Before you head out, the museum store is a great stop that is filled with art-inspired books, jewelry, and gifts.

There’s also Gertrude’s restaurant and bar on-site if you want a bite or a drink before or after exploring the galleries.

Note: there’s also a quiet room available for visitors if they need a space to nurse, pray or have a quiet moment.

The Cone Sisters Collection at the Baltimore Museum of Art is an absolute treasure. You can truly feel the passion, vision, and bold taste of the Cone sisters in every room. Their dedication to collecting modern art long before it was widely appreciated created a legacy that continues to inspire visitors today.
The collection features incredible works by Picasso, Van Gogh and many other influential artists, but what makes it special is the sense that its  almost as if you’re stepping into the world of two women who saw beauty and value where others hadn’t yet noticed it.
If you are in Baltimore, the Cone Sisters Collection alone is worth the trip. A must-see for anyone who loves art, history, or stories of strong women with visionary taste.

Came here for my girls work event and we had such a fun time. The atmosphere was so unique and nostalgic 👌

Staff were extremely friendly and the content that the museum provided was so informative! Great place to bring kids to learn about history from not so long ago. There was a handful of interactive exhibits that gets you engaging which is nice.

10/10 would recommend

This is definitely a must-see in Baltimore. It listed the history and industry of Baltimore, showing how those things worked back in the old days. And this is a very great location to take pictures over the water. If you want to know and feel the history of Baltimore and the country, this is the place!

A great place to explore while visiting Baltimore and learn the history of several industrial and manufacturing innovations. Tickets are priced well and it was easy to order one online. I came on a week day (though a federal holiday) in the afternoon and while there were several other people there, it was not crowded. I opted for the self-guided audio tour which was nice to stay at my own pace. I would love to come back again.

We visited during a community free admission day, and it was a wonderful visit! Even living here in the city, I find the museum somewhat hard to describe -- it's about industry, yes, but I think I would think about it more like a history museum of Baltimore with a specific slant to it. My personal favorite was the exhibit related to printing; if you visit on a weekend they have a working 1930 linotype machine! (The linotype machine was designed here in Baltimore, and revolutionized the printing process.) The volunteers were so kind about answering so many of our inane questions. I also liked the Domino Sugar sign remnant, which is positioned right in contrast to the current signage in the window, which is fun. The museum complex itself is very cool, too; it's a former oyster cannery but it's got beautiful views right on the waterfront.
Many things to read and learn. Free audio tour adds really nice insight into what you're seeing. Staff is helpful and will answer questions about the exhibit. I recommend for adults.

museums.content_summary: The Baltimore Museum of Industry invites visitors to explore the rich tapestry of Baltimore's industrial heritage. Engaging exhibits bring history to life, showcasing the vital role of workers and industries in shaping the city. Experience hands-on activities and interactive displays that make the past resonate today.
museums.content_description: **The Baltimore Museum of Industry (BMI)** stands as a testament to the city’s dynamic industrial past, illustrating the profound impact of the workforce on Baltimore’s development. Nestled on the waterfront, the museum occupies a historic 1860s industrial complex, providing an authentic backdrop that immerses guests in the sights and sounds of yesteryear. From shipbuilding to manufacturing, **BMI** captures the essence of industries that fueled the city’s growth, offering a unique glimpse into the lives of the laborers who contributed to the city’s identity. Visitors will be captivated by the real machinery, tools, and artifacts that fill the exhibits, offering an engaging, tactile experience of Baltimore’s evolving landscape.  In addition to its extensive collections, the museum is renowned for its interactive exhibits, allowing visitors, especially children, to touch and engage with history in a way that sparks curiosity and wonder.  Hands-on activities, such as operating a miniature factory or participating in craft demonstrations, put the industrial process directly into the hands of visitors, ensuring memorable experiences for all.  The museum not only showcases the history of production and labor but also tells the stories of the workers, reinforcing the relationship between the labor force and the industries that spurred growth in the city.  Beyond the exhibitions, the picturesque harbor and historic surroundings create an inviting atmosphere for visitors to reflect on the past while enjoying the vibrant present of Baltimore.  The **Baltimore Museum of Industry** is truly a remarkable destination for anyone ready to see, hear, and touch the intricate history of a city built by its industrious people.
content_highlights: Interactive exhibits demonstrating historical manufacturing processes
Original machinery and tools from Baltimore's industrial past
Hands-on activities for children and families
Historic waterfront location with stunning views
Showcases the stories of the workers who shaped the city

museums.content_summary: The Captain Avery Museum in Shady Side is a hidden treasure that offers a unique glimpse into Maryland's maritime history and the legacy of its local community. Embedded in a historic waterfront setting, this museum captures the essence of the region's seafaring past, making it a must-visit for history enthusiasts and families alike.
museums.content_description:
**The Captain Avery Museum** allows visitors to truly immerse themselves in the rich maritime heritage of the Chesapeake Bay region. Housed in a quaint, historic building that dates back to the early 1900s, this museum serves as a gateway to the tales of local watermen, shipbuilders, and the intricate relationship between the community and the water. With its scenic views of the bay and charming nautical décor, the museum transports guests to a time when the waters were teeming with life and adventure. This experience is not just about observing; it's about experiencing Baltimore's maritime story firsthand.  

Visitors can explore intriguing exhibits that feature *artifacts*, photographs, and personal stories that illuminate the everyday lives of those who lived and worked on the water. The museum's collections speak to a diverse range of topics, from the evolution of boatbuilding techniques to the impact of the seafood industry on local culture. **Special events**, including educational workshops and seasonal festivals, add vibrancy to the museum experience, encouraging community interaction and making each visit unique. As you navigate through the museum, you'll discover the profound connection between Baltimore and its waterways, leaving you with a deeper appreciation for this historic region. Immerse yourself in the stories, sights, and sounds of the Chesapeake at **Captain Avery Museum**.
content_highlights: Intimate maritime history exhibits showcasing local watermen's stories
Historic building offering scenic views of the Chesapeake Bay
Engaging community events and workshops throughout the year
Unique artifacts related to the history of boatbuilding
Rich cultural narratives connecting Baltimore to its waterways

museums.content_summary: Experience the rich history of colonial Maryland at the Hammond-Harwood House, a stunning example of 18th-century architecture and a treasure trove of period decorative arts. This historic gem invites visitors to step back in time and explore the lives of those who shaped Annapolis and American history.
museums.content_description: **Hammond-Harwood House** stands as a quintessential landmark of colonial Maryland, offering visitors a window into the lifestyle and craftsmanship of the 18th century. Built in 1774, this stunning mansion showcases the exquisite Georgian architectural style, with its intricate detail and **symmetrical elegance**. As you explore the home, take in the carefully preserved interiors adorned with period furniture, *fine arts*, and decorative objects that reflect the tastes and aspirations of the colonial gentry. The house's design is often hailed as one of the best examples of the work of architect **William Buckland**, making it a must-see for those interested in American architecture and history. The harmonious blend of beauty and practicality that defines the house invites exploration and appreciation of its artistry.  As you wander through the rooms, consider the stories that each piece of furniture and artwork carries—each item reflects the culture, trade, and social dynamics of a developing nation.  The museum also offers guided tours led by knowledgeable staff who bring the past to life through insightful narratives about the home’s original inhabitants, the **Hammond and Harwood families**, and their role within their community.  Visitors can expect an immersive experience that transcends mere observation, allowing them to engage with Maryland's rich history through knowledgeable interactions and breathtaking artistry.  Perhaps one of the most remarkable aspects of the **Hammond-Harwood House** is its commitment to preservation, showcasing the importance of historical conservation in maintaining the legacy of America's architectural heritage.
content_highlights: Exquisite Georgian architecture and design elements
Insightful guided tours that bring history to life
A collection of original 18th-century furniture and decorative arts
Engagement with stories of colonial life in Maryland
Significant contributions to the preservation of American heritage

museums.content_summary: A must-stop on Havre de Grace’s waterfront, the Havre de Grace Decoy Museum celebrates the Chesapeake Bay’s most distinctive art form: hand-carved hunting decoys. More than folk craft, these birds are sculptural portraits—painted with keen observation and regional flair. With an intimate, local feel and a focused collection, the museum rewards close looking, whether you’re drawn to coastal traditions, American vernacular art, or the quiet beauty of working objects made with extraordinary skill.
museums.content_description:
**Havre de Grace Decoy Museum** is a small but richly characterful destination for art lovers curious about the Chesapeake’s homegrown sculptural tradition. Here, waterfowl decoys—once essential tools for hunting—are presented as works of **American folk art**, where carving, paint, and keen natural observation come together in tactile, elegant form. Expect to see a range of bird types and carving approaches, from crisp, streamlined silhouettes to more fully modeled bodies with expressive heads and subtle surface detailing—an ideal setting for appreciating *vernacular sculpture* up close.

The museum’s strength is its **focused collection** and the way it reveals how local makers translated the Bay’s ecology into art. For visitors attuned to material and technique, the appeal lies in the craftsmanship: tool marks that remain visible, carefully layered paint, and the distinct “hand” of individual carvers. Even without blockbuster scale, the displays invite slow looking—comparing profiles, studying how a decoy’s balance suggests buoyancy, and noticing how regional preferences shape form and finish.

Set in walkable Havre de Grace near the water, the visitor experience feels personal and accessible. Plan on a compact, satisfying visit that pairs beautifully with the town’s maritime atmosphere: see the objects inside, then step outdoors to the landscapes that inspired them. It’s an art museum visit in miniature—intimate, specific, and deeply tied to place.
content_highlights: Hand-carved Chesapeake Bay waterfowl decoys presented as American folk-art sculpture
Close-range viewing that rewards attention to carving techniques, tool marks, and painted surface finish
A focused, local collection that connects artistry to the region’s maritime and hunting heritage
Compact galleries ideal for a short, high-impact stop on a Havre de Grace day trip
A strong sense of place—pair the visit with waterfront walks to understand the Bay’s visual inspiration

So the museum isn't just about decoys but also tells a lot of the story of the local area.  And the decoys on display are art.  So it is a art museum and a history museum.

The immersive experience continues with hands-on activities and programs designed for families and children, ensuring that every visitor can connect with history in a meaningful way.  ** _Immerse yourself in the stories that shaped our nation_ and be inspired by the dedication to preserving this essential landmark. Located two blocks from Inner Harbor in Downtown Baltimore, the Reginald F. Lewis Museum of Maryland African American History & Culture – a Smithsonian Affiliate – documents, interprets, and preserves the complex experiences, contributions, and culture of Black people. The Lewis Museum serves as a catalyst of sustained change by providing robust programs and exhibitions and bold conversations that educate and challenge. We strive to be a trusted custodian, a respected authority, and a thought-partner on the history, art and culture of the African diaspora with an emphasis on the State of Maryland.

Founded in 2005, the 82,000-square-foot facility accommodates over 13,000 square feet of permanent and temporary exhibition space, hosting more than 11,000 objects in our permanent collection, special exhibitions, educational programs, and public events.

Mission: The Reginald F. Lewis Museum documents, interprets and preserves the complex experiences, contributions and culture of Black people in Maryland. We serve as a catalyst for sustained change by providing programs, exhibitions and bold conversations that educate and challenge.

google_reviews.text: We're wedding photographers based in Washington, DC, but we recently got the chance to document a marriage celebration at The Ward Museum for Wildfowl Art. Schumaker Pond is absolutely lovely, and the trail that runs around it offers so many picturesque spots that we could spend hours there taking wedding portraits and not run out of beautiful backdrops. The main outdoor ceremony space on a lawn behind the main museum building gives you the chance to exchange your vows with a gorgeous view of Schumaker Pond stretching behind you. The huge windows that comprise one wall of the indoor reception area also give you a great look at the pond, as well as an opportunity to see a nice sunset if the weather cooperates!

We went to the museum on a Saturday morning right after they opened. Their award winning carvings are some of the best I've ever seen. It took us about 2 hours to go through the museum and the volunteer was their to offer us assistance and provide information. They have a nice outside area with sculptures and a walking trail. I highly recommend this museum for anyone who enjoys exquisitely detailed wood carving.

You can also buy handmade art in their gift shop from just a couple bucks for a hand painted bookmark to thousands for a lifelike bird carving.

Small, but fun day trip. Very informative center, and thorough explanations of art work. The museum is very focused on the bird hunting culture of Delmarva. The small trail had great scenery, a good way to spend an afternoon.

Showcases the art (both decoy and traditional paintings) of Lem and Steve Ward.

Programming such as talks and community events that add context and deepen engagement with the art
A walkable Easton setting that pairs naturally with a relaxed, itinerary-friendly museum day

google_reviews.text: Beautiful exhibition. Staff were so welcoming! I didn't take pictures of the KIN exhibit it was spiritual it was so moving. The book was available to take home. As a genealogist it speaks so much to me.
Very cool small (and admission free!) museum.  Exhibits change frequently so always worth a visit!

Rented space for my daughter's 9th birthday party. Fabulous staff, nice space, fun activity, low-stress party! Big hit with the kids and their parents! A real find! I can't comment on the rest of the building as it was under renovation at that time, but I'm sure had it been complete it would have been a nice bonus to our event. A talented artist artists named Theresa guided the kids on painting the subject matter of the birthday girl's choosing. She made it easy to follow, there were plenty of materials on hand, and she was excellent with the kids. I hadn't even known this space was available to rent for an event and I am so glad someone told me! We had a fabulous time. The staff and coordinators were very in touch for planning and questions and were extremely accommodating.

There was a deposit for renting the space and then I think it was $5 per person who would be painting (for the materials). They gave them real canvas to use, painters pencils, provided paint brush and paints, and smocks as well. They also provided space for food setup, provided the flatware, and did the cleanup. We had to provide food but they had a small fridge and freezer for cake and ice cream storage. When some of the kids were done with their painting and the others were not she provided paper and things for freestyle drawing to occupy the kids while the others finished up without any cost. So worth it!

BLUF: I recommend.
The parking is all street parking.
I do NOT recommend bringing walking babies, toddlers, or kindergarten aged kids here.  There are too many temptations to touch things that are NOT touchable.  Parents save your sanity and leave young kids with a babysitter!

I had a wonderful time going through this smaller but packed art museum.  My husband and kids were bored after running through it HOWEVER they aren't ones to stop and stare at art.

For anyone looking for a unique place to hold a wedding or mature birthday party and NOT decorating, this would be a very good place, except for the street parking.  It's a big issue to me. LoL

If you plan to take your kids and they aren't big art fans, I'd check the website to see when the museum is offering kid friendly classes.  That may make the trip a bit more enjoyable for them.  I know my kids wouldn't mind coming back but only if they can touch something or do an art class.

Bottom line, I recommend.
Cross stitch collection was great! The Bugatti exhibit was really interesting.

museums.content_summary: A cultural anchor in Hagerstown’s leafy City Park, the Washington County Museum of Fine Arts rewards art lovers with an intimate, thoughtfully curated visit—free admission included. Expect a strong regional lens alongside European and American painting, works on paper, and sculpture presented at an approachable scale. It’s the kind of museum where you can slow down with a single canvas, chat with staff who know the collection, and step back outside to gardens and park views between galleries.
museums.content_description:
**Washington County Museum of Fine Arts** is a destination museum in miniature—serious enough for devoted art travelers, yet relaxed enough to feel like a local secret. Set within Hagerstown’s City Park, it offers the pleasure of close-looking without the crowds: galleries where you can take your time with **American and European painting, prints and drawings, and sculpture**, often with a welcome emphasis on the Mid-Atlantic’s cultural landscape. With a **competently curated, modest collection**, the museum shines through smart rotations and clear interpretation, making it easy to connect individual works to broader stories in *portraiture*, *landscape*, and modern shifts in style and technique.

Architecturally, the museum’s **classical, civic-minded building** suits its mission—art as a public good—while its park setting adds a distinctly travel-worthy atmosphere. Plan to move at an unhurried pace: the scale encourages repeat visits and careful comparison across mediums, from the crisp line of works on paper to the material presence of sculpture.

For visitors, the experience is as much about rhythm as it is about highlights: arrive, focus in the galleries, then reset outdoors with views of trees, paths, and seasonal color before returning for another room. If you love museums where the pleasures are **concentration, discovery, and local context**, this is an ideal stop on a Maryland art itinerary—especially when paired with Hagerstown’s historic downtown nearby.
content_highlights: Free-admission, art-lover-friendly museum experience in Hagerstown’s City Park setting
Core strengths in American and European painting alongside prints, drawings, and sculpture
Thoughtful, accessible curation that supports slow looking and repeat visits
Classically styled museum building with a civic, public-art character
Easy to combine with a stroll through the park and a short visit to downtown Hagerstown

google_reviews.text:
Hubby and I had planned to go into Baltimore to the local museum, but it is closed Tuesdays. While searching for a new destination, we found this museum and it did not disappoint.

Parking was free and right out front. Steps later we were indoors and greeted by their delightful and informative staff. Entrance was free. We were given a map for self tour. The exhibits were well taken care of and inspirational. Total time to see everything was 1.5 hours. The Scandinavian exhibit is their new one.

Loved the local artist exhibit and reading their inspiration for each piece and getting a chance to vote on them.

Outside is the city park which was fun to walk around (just watch your step - lots of geese).

Also, the gift shop was a nice addition where I purchased a beautiful pitcher for $20.

This is my first time visiting the fine arts museum, and I definitely enjoyed my time there. It's free admission, and the staff is very welcoming. I visited early Sunday afternoon so I basically had the museum to myself. The museum itself is a square and not hard to navigate at all. They have a gift shop and plenty of places to sit throughout the galleries. They also showcase local talent.
Wouldn't recommend going with younger children. I saw a family come with their two children, and they spent the majority of the time chasing them around.

A true cultural treasure in the heart of Hagerstown! The Washington County Museum of Fine Arts is hands-down one of the finest small museums I’ve ever visited—and best of all, admission is completely free! Housed in a beautiful historic building right on the edge of Hagerstown City Park, the museum punches way above its weight with an impressive permanent collection that includes American masters like Childe Hassam, Mary Cassatt, Thomas Hart Benton, and even a stunning Tiffany glass vase. The Hudson River School landscapes and the intimate gallery of Old Masters are personal favorites.

The rotating exhibitions are always thoughtfully curated and surprisingly ambitious—recent shows have featured everything from contemporary photography to vintage fashion to major traveling exhibits you’d expect to see in D.C. or Baltimore. The staff and docents are warm, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate; they make every visit feel special.

Bonus highlights:
- The Singer Memorial Gallery with its soaring ceiling and natural light is breathtaking.
- The outdoor sculpture garden is perfect for a quiet moment.
- Family-friendly activities, fantastic children’s programs, and the summer concert series on the lawn are pure joy.
- Spotless facilities, free parking, and a lovely little gift shop with unique items.

Whether you’re an art lover or just looking for a peaceful, inspiring way to spend an hour or two, this museum is an absolute gem. Five stars isn’t enough!

I went for the floating beauty exhibit, but ended up going through all other exhibits. The museum is not big, but it is nicely organized with lots of fun items ranging from its own collection of Japanese prints, Chinese bronze and pottery items, Native American crafts, African crafts to Rodin’s sculpture, paintings, drawings, Wedgwood tea pots, and a painting attributed to Titian. The American arts works are arrange to cover both classical works to modern works. I also found a painting by Alfred Stieglitz. The E.O Hoppe photography exhibit of Women’s portraits are equally great! I really enjoyed everything in the museum. The staff are super friendly. I think the city is lucky to have a fine Art museum in the city park and everyone shop at the nearby outlets should make a stop at the museum as a routine. I really appreciate it!
Many areas were under construction but it was still very enjoyable, beautiful exhibits and friendly staff!

museums.content_summary: The Pyramid Atlantic Arts Center is a vibrant hub of creativity located in Silver Spring, Maryland, offering visitors an immersive experience that celebrates the intersection of art and craftsmanship. Known for its unique workshops and exhibitions, the center invites you to explore contemporary printmaking, book arts, and papermaking in a hands-on environment that inspires imagination.
museums.content_description: **Pyramid Atlantic Arts Center** stands as a beacon of artistic innovation in Silver Spring, Maryland. This dynamic cultural space is dedicated to the exploration of printmaking, paper arts, and the written word, merging traditional techniques with modern artistic expression. Here, you will find a welcoming atmosphere that invites both seasoned artists and curious novices to participate in a diverse range of workshops and community events. Visitors can witness the art-making process up close and even engage in hands-on activities that foster a deeper appreciation for these unique mediums. It’s about more than just viewing; it’s about experiencing art in a tactile way. Whether you’re interested in learning how to create your own prints or simply observing artists at work, **Pyramid Atlantic** offers a unique blend of education and inspiration. As you walk through the center, you will find exhibitions that consistently showcase local and national artists, reflecting the vibrant artistic community of the area. The building itself is a transformed industrial space, a perfect backdrop for the contemporary works that it houses, infused with an atmosphere of creativity and collaboration. The architectural features, including exposed brick and open studio areas, provide a warm and inviting environment where art enthusiasts of all ages can thrive. A visit to **Pyramid Atlantic Arts Center** is not just a trip to see art; it’s an invitation to *create*, *learn*, and *engage* with the art-making process in unforgettable ways.
content_highlights: Interactive workshops in printmaking and papermaking
Regular exhibitions featuring local and national artists
Community-focused programs and events
Stunning industrial architecture with art-making studios
Unique art shop showcasing one-of-a-kind artist prints and materials

google_reviews.text: Historical building, friendly and knowledgeable staff, had a free art exhibit upstairs that was a wonderful experience. Picked up some lovely prints. If we were local I would sign up for one of their printing classes.

You need to visit here! They have rotating exhibits in their gorgeous gallery space upstairs, a working studio with classes available to the public (I've taken letterpress classes, which are SO fun), and the most gorgeous gift shop. The people are lovely and you get great advance info if you become a member!

Such a cool arts center! I took my first class there.  It won't be my last.  The instructor was knowledgeable and made the class fun. The other participants were interesting which made the class even more fun. Highly recommend.
The gallery and the space is great. Love this place.

I thought the place was amazing, was there for a guided tour and was amazed at all of the different types of printing and book making contraptions. I loved that they offer classes on all of their equipment and once you are certified you are free to create. The upstairs gallery is pretty tiny though i will admit. I think they should really think about expanding that area. It kinda has a jail cell feel. Not that I would know anything about that. The staff inside are very friendly and welcoming. The artist that are inside are not stingy with their art style or knowledge and are willing to share their ideas. I really loved the artist for that.  Small gallery yeah but all everything else in my opinion gave this shop a 5 of 5 stars.
